chapter: The Four Seasons and Bob Crewe
title: Meeting Frankie Valli through his arrangements
summary: Musicians valued his arrangements; Frankie Valli heard his five-piece vocal band and recruited him for The Four Lovers.

story.theme_name: First paying gigs: getting started as a young professional
story.community_name: First paid gigs: pay, bands and young beginnings

blocks.x: Well one of the things that I learned later on was I was not a great player. But musicians loved the arrangements and I knew how to make the arrangements sound great because of the accordion, because I could harmonize and play the in-between notes with the accordion so the chords would always sound full. And that was basically how I met Frankie Valli. He came into a club that I was working in. I had graduated high school. I was going to Manhattan School of Music and still working with a band. And he walked into a club, heard the band, and said, “Who wrote the arrangements?” And they pointed to me. And as a result of me getting to know Frankie Valli ultimately I had opportunity. © Fillius Jazz Archive -3-
What did he particularly notice? Because -- did you have horn players? How large was the band?

The band was five pieces. We had a trumpet player who played valve trombone and trumpet; and we had an alto player who played tenor; we had Fender bass, drums, and I played the accordion. So we also sang like the Four Freshmen and the Hi-Lo’s. Now I copied some of the arrangements off the record. The first one we started with was “It’s a Blue World,” which was relatively easy, especially ‘cause all the people in the band went to Arts High, they were all good musicians, they could read music, and as a result of it we could sing. So we rehearsed and we found out that we could actually sing and get a sound like the Four Freshmen. And then we did some of the tunes from the Hi-Lo’s. So Frankie comes in, here’s this band that was doing production numbers with two horns and also singing four part harmony. And he had a band called the Four Lovers. They had a hit record, or a chart record, on RCA in 1956. So everybody knew who Frankie Valli was in the city of Newark. But he had heard about my band, came to hear the band, and was amazed at how we sounded. So Frankie wanted me to join The Four Lovers. So I continued – I wanted to continue to go to school so I quit the band I was in and went to work with Frankie Valli and The Four Lovers playing bass. And the music that they did was sort of uninspiring and they didn’t want to rehearse or change. They didn’t have the musicality to do the things that we were doing with the other band. What was funny about it was all the musicians in town knew who we were. The name of the group was The Victorians. We couldn’t draw six people. Frankie Valli played, they had a triad band that played like four chord songs and you couldn’t get into the place.
